1.
Call to Order
2.

NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC FOR CLOSED SESSION
Prior to going into closed session, the City Council will convene in the Auditorium serving as Council Chambers to take public comment on the closed session items only. General public comment will be provided for during the regular portion of the meeting beginning at 7:30 P.M.
1.
CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATORS ? Pursuant to California Government Code, Section 54957.6 City Negotiator: Sergio Gonzalez, City Manager, Talika M. Johnson, Director of Administrative Services and Nico De Anda-Scaia, Deputy City Manager.
Organizations: IBEW (International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers - Local 18), APMA (Azusa Police Management Association), and APEA (Azusa Police Executive Association).
2.
PUBLIC EMPLOYEE DISCIPLINE/DISMISSAL/RELEASE ? Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957
7:30 P.M. - REGULAR MEETING OF THE CITY COUNCIL
NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC FOR REGULAR MEETING
Copies of staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business referred to on the Agenda are on file in the Office of the City Clerk and are available for public inspection at the City Library.
Persons who wish to speak during the Public Participation portion of the Agenda, shall fill out a card requesting to speak and shall submit it to the City Clerk prior to the start of the City Council meeting. When called, each person may address any item on or off the agenda during the public participation.
In compliance with Government Code Section 54957.5, copies of staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business referred to on the Agenda are on file in the Office of the City Clerk - 213 E. Foothill Blvd.; copies for public view are at the Azusa City Library - 729 N. Dalton Ave., Azusa Police Department Lobby - 725 N. Alameda Ave., and the City of Azusa Web Page www.azusaca.gov. Persons who wish to speak in-person during the Public Participation portion of the Agenda or on a Public Hearing item shall fill out a card requesting to speak and shall submit it to the City Clerk prior to 7:30 P.M.; cards submitted after this time will not be accepted.
Those wishing to participate during Public Comment may do so in-person at the Azusa Auditorium, or may submit written public comments by emailing PublicComment@azusaca.gov. Emailed public comments are due by 5:30 p.m. and shall be limited to no more than 250 words. Written public comments will be provided to the City Council and will be part of the record but will not be read aloud.
View the City Council meeting live on the City’s website https://www.ci.azusa.ca.us/1389/Watch-Meetings-Online, or on Channel 3 (Spectrum). Archived video of recorded meetings is also available on the City website.
Notice Regarding California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determinations. Pursuant to CEQA, a "project" is defined as a "whole action" subject to a public agency's discretionary funding or approval that has the potential to either (1) cause a direct physical change in the environment or (2) cause a reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment. "Projects" include discretionary activity by a public agency, a private activity that receives any public funding, or activities that involve the public agency's issuance of a discretionary approval and is not statutorily or categorically exempt from CEQA. (Pub. Res. Code § 21065.)   To the extent that matters listed in this Agenda are considered “projects” under CEQA, their appropriate CEQA determination will be listed below each recommendation.  If no CEQA determination is listed, it has been determined that the action does not constitute a “project” under CEQA.

B.
PUBLIC PARTICIPATION
This time has been set aside for persons in the audience to make public comments on items listed or not listed on this Agenda. Members of the audience will have the opportunity to address the City Council/Agency Board about public hearing items at the time the public hearing is held. Under the provisions of the Brown Act, the Council/Agency Board is prohibited from taking action on oral requests, but may refer the matter to staff or to a subsequent meeting. Each person or representative of a group shall be allowed to speak without interruption for up to five (5) continuous minutes, subject to compliance with applicable meeting rules. Questions to the speaker or responses to the speaker's questions or comments may be handled after the speaker has completed his/her comments. Public Participation will be limited to sixty (60) minutes.
C.

PUBLIC HEARING - DELINQUENT TRASH COLLECTION FEES
RECOMMENDED ACTION: 1) Open the Public Hearing, receive public testimony, and close the Public Hearing; and

individually, it will be considered under SPECIAL CALL ITEMS.

CITY OF AZUSA

  MINUTES OF THE CITY COUNCIL, THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY
  TO THE FORMER REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY,
  THE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY
  REGULAR MEETING
  MONDAY, JUNE 16, 2025

 The City Council of the City of Azusa met in Closed and Regular session at Azusa Auditorium at 213 E.
 Foothill Blvd., Azusa, CA 91702.

 Mayor Gonzales called the meeting to order at 6:30 P.M.

 ROLL CALL: Roll call was taken by City Clerk Cornejo.

 PRESENT: COUNCILMEMBERS: GONZALES, ALVAREZ, AVILA, MENDEZ, BOW
 ABSENT: COUNCILMEMBERS: NONE

 ALSO PRESENT

 Elected Officials: City Clerk Cornejo

 Staff Members: City Manager Gonzalez, Director of Administrative Services Johnson, Deputy City Manager
 De Anda-Scaia, City Attorney Martinez

 PUBLIC COMMENT - None

 CLOSED SESSION

 The City Council recessed to closed session at 6:31 p.m. to discuss the following items:

 1. CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATORS – Pursuant to California Government Code, Section
 54957.6
  City Negotiator: Sergio Gonzalez, City Manager, Talika M. Johnson, Director of Administrative
 Services and Nico De Anda-Scaia, Deputy City Manager
  Organizations:  IBEW (International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers - Local 18), APMA
 (Azusa Police Management Association), and APEA (Azusa Police Executive Association).

 2. PUBLIC EMPLOYEE DISCIPLINE/DISMISSAL/RELEASE – Pursuant to California Government Code
 Section 54957

 REGULAR SESSION

 Mayor Gonzales called the meeting to order at 7:30 P.M.

 ROLL CALL: Roll call was taken by City Clerk Cornejo.

 PRESENT: COUNCILMEMBERS: GONZALES, ALVAREZ, AVILA, MENDEZ, BOW
 ABSENT: COUNCILMEMBERS: NONE

City Council Minutes  Page | 1
June 16, 2025
  ALSO PRESENT

 Elected Officials: City Clerk Cornejo

 Staff Members: City Manager Gonzalez, City Attorney Martinez, Deputy City Manager DeAnda-Scaia,
 Director of Administrative Services Johnson, Chief of Police Wenrick, Administrative Seargent Beaver,
 Director of Community Resources Carpenter, Economic & Community Development Director Jimenez, City
 Clerk Services Manager Juarez, Environmental Programs Specialist Sagun, Economic and Community
 Development Director Jimenez, Budget Administrator Lam, Library Services Manager Hassen, Director of
 Public Works Delgadillo, Environmental Programs Manager Reid, Utilities Administrative and Financial
 Services Manager Smith, Assistant Director of Utilities- Costumer Care & Solutions Homes, Assistant
 Director – Resource Management Torres, General Manager of Utilities Singh.

 The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Ms. Laura Nawaya.

 The Invocation was led by Adrian Greer, Foothill Community Church.

 CLOSED SESSION

 City Attorney Martinez announced the following regarding Closed Session: All members were present; the
 City Council heard a presentation from its negotiating team, provided direction; and there was no reportable
 action.

 CEREMONIAL

 1.  Presentation of Proclamation proclaiming the Month of June 2025 as LGBTQ+ Pride Month in the City
 of Azusa

 Mayor Gonzales presented the proclamation in honor of LGBTQ+ Pride Month.

 PUBLIC PARTICIPATION

 Bruce Monroe addressed Item D-3, expressing his support of the motive for the ban; and suggested that the
 ban be regulated by age and speed of the bike.

 The following individuals expressed concern regarding the absence of spay/neuter and microchipping
 requirements in Azusa; noted the high number of offspring a single animal can produce; emphasized that
 increased intake at shelters often results in animals being euthanized; and urged the Council to consider
 mandating spaying, neutering, and microchipping of pets: Tom Kiesche, Veronica Menjivar, Robert Arnold,
 and Alex Charlier.

 Ernesto Macias, Vice President of Tree Service Kings, expressed concern regarding the outcome of the recent
 Citywide Tree Maintenance Contract bid process; stated that rejecting all bids created an unbalanced
 outcome; requested that the Council direct Staff to review all submitted bids for responsiveness; and asked the
 Council to reconsider their decision.

 REPORTS, UPDATES, AND ANNOUNCEMENTS FROM STAFF/COUNCIL

 1.City Manager Communications

 City Manager Gonzalez announced that Staff requested to pull Item E-5 from the agenda to address
 housekeeping items and defer action until it is brought back to Council; and reminded the Council that July
 21st will be the first and only meeting in July and will feature the annual Al Fresco event in the courtyard.

 2.‘Pet of the Month’ Presentation by Los Angeles County Animal Care & Control.

 Officer Arrighi–Bracci from the Los Angeles County Animal Care & Control Office introduced Socks, a
 seven-month-old Labrador/Pitbull mix at the Baldwin Park Animal Care Shelter; and provided background
 information on the animal and announced that he is ready for adoption.

City Council Minutes  Page | 2
June 16, 2025
  3.  Azusa Chamber of Commerce Presentation

 Jenny Bolivar, Executive Director of the Azusa Chamber of Commerce, recognized the 18 newly appointed
 Board Members following a year of dormancy; noted that the Chamber is now active and in good standing;
 announced four upcoming signature events: Wine Walk, Taste of the Town, Installation and Awards
 Ceremony, and the Holiday for Heroes Luncheon; also announced a Chamber membership drive and
 community relaunch event scheduled for Thursday, July 17, at the Azusa Greens Golf Course.
 4. Councilmember Announcements.

 Mayor Pro Tem Alvarez announced upcoming Library summer events; shared the line up for the 2025
 Summer Concert Series at Memorial Park; shared that he attended the 102nd birthday celebration of resident
 Elsie Contreras; and offered condolences to Officer Mario Gutierrez on the passing of his father.

 Councilmember Avila reported on upcoming Library events; thanked attendees of the Flag Retirement
 Ceremony; and thanked VFW 8070, American Legion 180, and the Southland Young Marines, for assisting
 with the proper retirement of flags.

 Councilmember Mendez congratulated the new Chamber of Commerce; reported attending the 100-year
 anniversary of Slauson Pool event over the weekend; and announced that he attended the 102nd birthday
 celebration for resident Elsie Contreras.

 Councilmember Bow announced the upcoming Electronic Waste Drop-Off on June 21 at the Public Works
 Yard; reported attending her first Flag Retirement Ceremony; and shared that she attended both the birthday
 celebration for Elsie Contreras and the Splash into Summer event celebrating 100 years of Slauson Pool.

 Mayor Gonzales thanked Community Resources Staff for their work on the Splash into Summer event; and
 reminded the community that illegal fireworks are prohibited, with fines beginning at $1,000.

 SCHEDULED ITEMS

 1. PUBLIC HEARING - DELINQUENT TRASH COLLECTION FEES

 Environmental Program Specialist Sagun requested Council’s approval of a list of delinquent accounts to be
 placed on special assessment and included in the Los Angeles County Assessor’s property tax roll for Fiscal
 Year 2025–2026; provided a reminder of the ordinance with Athens Services, which includes provisions for
 collecting delinquent accounts through the tax roll; and noted that this is the third year the City has held a
 public hearing on the matter.

 Sagun explained that three notices were sent to residents; 274 accounts were notified and as of the hearing
 date, the number of outstanding accounts had reduced to 105; explained that the unpaid collection fees total
 $75,875, which includes administrative costs; and announced that administrative fees will be reimbursed to
 the City to cover expenses associated with administering the ordinance and facilitating delinquent payments to
 Athens Services.

 Council expressed concerns regarding the notices sent to residents, noting that only one of the three appeared
 to have been received. Director of Government Affairs for Athens Services Amaya assured the Council that
 notices were distributed in February, April, and May.

 Mayor Gonzales opened the Public Hearing.

 City Clerk Cornejo certified the publication of the Public Hearing in the San Gabriel Valley Tribune on June
 3, 2025. There being no one wishing to address the council on this issue, Mayor Gonzales asked for a motion
 to close the public hearing.

 Moved by Councilmember Mendez, seconded by Councilmember Alvarez and carried unanimously by the
 following roll call vote of the Council to close the Public Hearing,

 AYES: GONZALES, ALVAREZ, AVILA, MENDEZ, BOW
 NOES: NONE
 ABSENT: NONE
 ABSTAIN: NONE

City Council Minutes  Page | 3
June 16, 2025
  Moved by Councilmember Mendez and seconded by Councilmember Avila and carried by unanimous vote of
 the Council to: Adopt Resolution No. 2025-C30 approving the list of delinquent accounts to be placed on
 special assessment for inclusion to the property tax roll by the Los Angeles County Assessor on the FY 2025-
 2026 tax bill; and authorize the Director of Administrative Services, or her designee, to turn over to the Los
 Angeles County Assessor the delinquent account list after the adoption of Resolution No. 2025-C30.

 AYES: GONZALES, ALVAREZ, AVILA, MENDEZ, BOW
 NOES: NONE
 ABSENT: NONE
 ABSTAIN: NONE

 Total Cost: N/A Is the Cost of this item budgeted? N/A
 Fund/Account No: N/A

 2.  ADOPTION OF FISCAL YEARS 2025-26 AND 2026-27 BIENNIAL BUDGET (ENDING JUNE 30,
 2027) FOR CITY, UTILITIES, PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY, AND SUCCESSOR AGENCY
 OPERATING AND CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PLAN AND REAFFIRM GENERAL FUND RESERVE
 POLICY

 City Manager Gonzalez thanked Staff for their hard work on the budget; reflected on Council’s vision and
 goals; emphasized the importance of improving City facilities, recreation programs, the Senior Center, and
 streets, while also highlighting the City’s commitment to public safety and the Police Department’s fleet lease
 program.

 Director of Administrative Services Johnson provided an overview of the Biennial Operating and Capital
 Improvement Budget; highlighted the City’s budget strategy, noting that the budget is developed by
 evaluating revenues, essential costs, community priorities, and overall fiscal capacity; and explained that the
 guiding principles include responsible spending, maintaining service quality, and ensuring long-term fiscal
 stability.

 Johnson also presented an Economic Overview, addressing key challenges such as rising labor costs and
 inflation in capital projects; and emphasized the City’s focus on preserving core services and aligning
 resources with the Council’s strategic goals.

 The General Fund budget, which serves as the City’s primary funding source for public safety and general
 administration was presented with Revenues for FY 2025–2026 were projected at $73 million, and $75.8
 million for FY 2026–2027; Expenditures were projected at $72.5 million for FY 2025–2026 and $75.4 million
 for FY 2026–2027, both representing balanced budgets; anticipated revenue growth such as increases in
 property tax due to higher property values; and FY 2025–2026 will be the first year the City begins to see
 revenue from Measure ZZ; departmental General Fund budgets remain flat, with increases primarily reflecting
 labor negotiations and higher Citywide insurance premiums; noted that staff continues to seek grant
 opportunities to help offset costs associated with the ARC; and explained that the City has adopted a General
 Fund Policy requiring annual review, and any use of General Fund reserves must be approved by Council.

 Johnson reviewed the Reserve Policy, recommending that the City Council reaffirm the current policy without
 changes and continue setting aside $3.5 million annually; reported that General Fund balances are projected to
 be just under $42 million for FY 2025–2026 and just over $42 million for FY 2026–2027; undesignated
 reserves are estimated at $4.5 million by the end of 2026 and $3.7 million by the end of 2027; and gave an
 overview of , Citywide proposed revenues, detailed capital outlays, Personnel FTE summary, and
 departmental proposals for new full-time positions and reclassifications.

 Director of Administrative Services Johnson concluded the presentation with a review of the Five-Year
 Capital Improvement Program; noting $94 million in projects, including the Farmers Market, Downtown
 Streetscape, and the San Gabriel two-way conversion; highlighted planned improvements across all
 departments; and emphasized that all budgets are balanced with strong excess reserves, and requested
 Council approval and adoption of the two-year budget.

 Council raised questions regarding the estimated amount of the Capital Improvement Program, totaling
 $93,775,265; expressed concern about the allocated funds for the Farmers Market project, which has not yet
 in fruition; and inquired whether the Chamber of Commerce could play a role in launching the Farmers
 Market.

 3.  FIRST READING - ORDINANCE AMENDING SECTION 46-321 AND 50-2 OF THE AZUSA
 MUNICIPAL CODE TO PROHIBIT THE USE OF E-BIKES AND MOTORIZED SCOOTERS IN PARKS,
 SIDEWALKS AND CITY RECREATIONAL AND GOVERNMENTAL FACILITIES

 Director of Community Resources, Carpenter presented the proposed ordinance prohibiting E-bikes and
 motorized scooters in all City parks, sidewalks, and public facilities, and restricting human-powered bicycles
 in parks unless signage permits use; noted that bicycles remain permitted on sidewalks except in front of
 churches, businesses, and shopping centers under existing regulations, and recommended waiving further
 reading of the ordinance.

 The Council requested clarification on the distinction between sidewalks and walking paths, inquired about
 possible age provisions, and expressed concern regarding safe areas for children to ride bicycles; and
 discussed whether provisions could be made for human-powered bicycles rather than an outright prohibition.

 Staff clarified that sidewalks and walking paths are not clearly distinguishable under current regulations;
 explained that bicycles are prohibited in parks unless signage allows otherwise; noted that the prohibition
 would also apply to walking paths and roadways without signage; indicated that adding age provisions would
 be difficult, emphasized the importance of consistent regulations for liability purposes; and highlighted that
 the City offers Bike Rodeos to promote bicycle safety. Discussion ensued regarding the possibility of further
 provisions.

 Moved by Councilmember Avila, seconded by Councilmember Alvarez, and carried by the following vote to
 Waive further reading, read by title only and introduce Ordinance No. 2025-04 entitled:

 4. TRANSITION OF PURCHASING/LEASING POLICE VEHICLES TO THE BANCORP FOR
 COMPREHENSIVE POLICE FLEET LEASING

 Administrative Sergeant, Beaver presented a proposal to transition from purchasing to leasing of police
 vehicles; outlined the current annual allocations of $506,848 for vehicles and $204,806.30 for radios, totaling
 $711,654.30; noted that vehicles currently last no more than three years; proposed moving to a
 comprehensive fleet leasing model with Bancorp, consolidating patrol, administrative, and detective vehicles
 into a single contract to provide cost savings and improved fleet management.

 Sergeant Beaver reviewed the budget for detective vehicles with no residual value and detailed the proposed
 process for leasing 30 fully equipped vehicles at $522,884.19 annually; explained that, upon lease expiration,
 residual value would be credited back to the City’s account for future leases, with an estimated return of
 $210,000; stated the proposal fits within the FY 2025–2026 adopted budget, locks in pricing for five years,
 and offers additional operational benefits.

 The Council expressed concern about the proposed five-year lease term given that current vehicles last only
 three years and inquired about how residual values were calculated. Staff explained that with 27 vehicles
 currently serving more than 50 officers on a 24-hour basis, vehicles tend to wear out quickly; further
 explained that leasing would allow for additional vehicles, reducing individual use and extending lifespan;
 and stated that Bancorp provided the residual estimates. There was discussion regarding differences between
 the City’s current provider, Enterprise, and the proposed provider, Bancorp, as well as warranties and
 maintenance provisions.

 Moved by Councilmember Avila, seconded by Councilmember Bow, and carried by the following vote of the
 Council to 1) Approve the comprehensive leasing plan with The Bancorp for all patrol, administrative, and
 detective vehicles; and 2) Authorize the City Manager or designee to execute the agreement, in a form
 acceptable to the City Attorney, on behalf of the City.

 AYES: GONZALES, ALVAREZ, AVILA, BOW
 NOES: MENDEZ
 ABSENT: NONE
 ABSTAIN: NONE
